note: D-172, corrected by D-192/D-193. THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT AN EXCUSE. Every entry below is a check that is RED on integrate/first-usable today. None of them is fixed here and none of them is suppressed: each one still runs in full on every push to the integration branch, from the quarantine-ratchet job of integration-gate.yml, and its findings are printed verbatim. What this file adds is the only thing a permanently-red step cannot give you -- a state that can FAIL. Each entry pins the SET OF FINDING IDENTITIES. scripts/ci/quarantine-ratchet.mjs fails if an id appears that is not listed, if a listed id disappears without this file being lowered in the same change, and -- the case D-192 was opened for -- if BOTH happen at once at an unchanged count.
note-D-192: The first version of this file pinned a COUNT and claimed, in this field, "Identical policy to scripts/ledger/state-baseline.json". That was false: scripts/ledger/all.mjs:28 reads "same count, different ids -> FAIL. One was fixed and one introduced." The D-172 adversary deleted the fail-closed guard at keyserver-cf/src/lib/auth.ts:38 -- a real authorization bypass, since constantTimeTokenEqual encodes `expected` with TextEncoder and `Bearer undefined` therefore authenticates when the comp secret is unset -- paired it with one plausible tidy-up (first.redeemed_at -> first?.redeemed_at), and the count returned to 13. The gate printed "still exactly 13, still quarantined" and "QUARANTINE RATCHET: HELD" with the bypass in the tree. It now pins identities, so that pair fails as DRIFT. The parity claim above is now true.
note-D-192-part-2: The vitest extractor read only the FAILED count, so a deleted, .skip-ped or uncollectable PASSING test was invisible and needed no compensating fix. Every vitest entry now also pins "metrics": the total number of tests collected, the total number of test FILES, and the number skipped. Breaking one import in a green cipher-store file -- the adversary's mutant -- moves tests 134 -> 133 and adds a "file [ file ]" id, and is now caught twice.
note-D-193: Three checks used to sit in "notRatcheted": a11y-overflow, cipher-store-tests-worker (219 tests) and keyserver-tests-node. All three were excluded from the ratchet AND executed by nothing -- an allowlist by another name -- and the keyserver-tests-node entry additionally claimed, in writing, to run "as its own step in the ts-test keyserver-worker lane". No such step existed. All three are now entries here, run by the quarantine-ratchet job, and graded by identity. Where a count genuinely moves without the code moving, the moving identity is named in "unstable" with its measurement, and everything else in the bucket is graded.

entries.why: Horizontal-overflow findings on /docs/compare, /docs/download and /docs/faq at 320px and 390px @200% zoom. D-193: this used to be in "notRatcheted" -- excluded from the ratchet and executed by nothing. The stated reason, that the finding count depends on the renderer, is true and is why "idsByEnvironment" exists; it is not a reason to stop running the check. The identity deliberately drops the pixel amount, which is the part that varies with the font stack, and keeps page + width + zoom, which is the finding. entries.whyEnvironmentDependent: Measured 6 findings on WSL/Chromium and 2 on ubuntu-latest/google-chrome from identical HTML (runs 30928896726 and 30929905893). The overflow is in pixels and the pixels depend on the installed font stack, so ONE pinned set would be a false red on the other machine and pinning nothing is what D-193 objected to. Each environment is graded against its own recorded set and an unrecorded environment is REFUSED, not waved through. The right permanent fix is to make the measurement reproducible -- a pinned font stack or a container -- after which this becomes a single "ids" array.

note-notRatcheted: Empty, and it must stay empty unless an entry here carries an "executedBy" naming the job that actually runs it. D-193: all three of the original entries were excluded from the ratchet AND executed by nothing, which is an allowlist by another name -- the one thing this project forbids outright. If a check truly cannot be ratcheted, it still has to RUN somewhere, and that somewhere has to be named and true.
